title: Article 44 — Uniform civil code for the citizens

content.overview: Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India. It is a Directive Principle — not a self-executing code of personal law.

sections.heading: Nature of the directive
sections.body: Article 44 is a policy goal addressed to the State. Personal laws continue until altered by competent legislation. Debates on uniformity engage Articles 14, 15, 25 and 26 as well — those are distinct, enforceable provisions.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Advise on the personal law or secular statute that actually governs the client's marriage, divorce, or succession. Do not treat Article 44 as an enacted uniform code.

sections.heading: Historical vs current
sections.body: HISTORICAL and political debate around a uniform civil code is long-standing. CURRENT LAW remains plural personal-law systems plus secular options such as the Special Marriage Act where applicable — subject to legislative change.
